title: Farm Real Estate Loans — Lateness Multiplier Applied to Late Charges
content:
**The rule.** The late charge on a Farm Real Estate Loans installment carries a lateness multiplier that follows how long the installment took to complete, in calendar days from its due date to the most recent scheduled principal payment: completed within 25 days, the charge is halved (multiplied by 0.5); completed more than 60 days after the due date, the charge is one and a half times the figure (multiplied by 1.5); otherwise it is the figure itself.

The figure multiplied is the unpaid part of the installment times the late-charge percentage; the multiplier acts on it before it is rounded to cents, and the result is then held to the product's minimum and maximum late charge.

## Questions the rule answers

**From which day is the completion counted?** From the due date, as day 0, to the effective date of the most recent scheduled principal payment.

**Is day 25 "within 25 days"?** Yes. Day 26 is not.

**Is day 60 "more than 60 days"?** No; the figure itself applies on day 60. Day 61 is more than 60 days.

## Ladder with hypothetical figures

Take a charge figure of 320.00 (an example input) on a product with a USD 50 minimum and USD 1500 maximum.

| Completed on | Multiplier | Charge |
|---|---|---|
| day 20 | 0.5 | 160.00 |
| day 25 | 0.5 | 160.00 |
| day 26 | 1 | 320.00 |
| day 60 | 1 | 320.00 |
| day 61 | 1.5 | 480.00 |

With a smaller figure of 36.00 completed on day 10, halving gives 18.00, which is then raised to the 50.00 minimum.
